transcript: Writer, performer, and trailblazer in theater accessibility Ryan J. Haddad is presenting a new piece at Playwrights Horizons and I loved it so, so much. It's a solo piece called Hold Me in the Water, and it's basically just Ryan telling the story of his first love. We learn how his cerebral palsy and its impact on his mobility intersects with his relationships. He recalls a sense of safety and access that one particular person provided him, seemingly effortlessly, and what that meant to him. As Ryan describes it, it's “when the practical become emotional.” And although there are plenty of universal nuggets of this story related to first loves and self-discovery, Ryan beautifully weaves in how the way he specifically navigates the world adds layers to these experiences. I had seen his last piece in New York, Dark Disabled Stories at The Public, which was great, but I think I enjoyed this even more. I thought it was so beautifully written and performed, and gloriously personal. He really has a way with words and his stage presence is wonderful too. The play is poetic, funny, vulnerable, raunchy, blunt, and charismatically conversational. I also loved how the ways that accessibility is integrated into this production not only support the mission of the piece, but are creatively or humorously used as theatrical devices as well. I think this piece will resonate with some more than others — it certainly resonated with me, but I would definitely recommend it to anyone and everyone. Hold Me in the Water is running at Playwrights Horizons into early May. With that another program for my collection.
